text:
Alexander Nikishin's season started on November 7, after a contract stalemate that ended with a one-year deal, and he has wasted no time. Four games, two goals, four points, including a power-play goal against Edmonton on Saturday. Four games is nothing to judge a season on, and two goals on four shots is finishing that won't last.

What's worth watching is everything around the points. Carolina has controlled play with him out there: 65% of the shot attempts and 68% of the expected goals at five on five. That's consistent with last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.7 wins above replacement, 36th among defensemen, with most of it from the power play. They also note he skated with very strong teammates, which flatters the raw on-ice numbers.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he's hard to beat at his own blue line (15% of entries at him stopped, typical 11%) and shoots plenty, though not often from the slot. The trade chatter hasn't stopped either: his name has appeared in rumor pieces linking him to Toronto and Detroit all month. For now, our range has him finishing around 28 points.
